messages:
sophie (support): heads up — ACME reported multiple users suddenly unable to access models and the billing page, escalation opened with their CSM. they say error is "permission denied" in console and 403s in API.

matt (eng-security): thanks. did this coincide with the RBAC refactor we rolled earlier?

elena (eng-platform): yep we deployed the rbac-refactor v2 at 09:18; I see a deploy bot note: ops-bot: deploy rbac-refactor v2 to prod by elena - 2024-04-30T09:18:22Z :rocket: 

carla (devex): ACME user logs show failures when calling model list and billing endpoints: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "access_denied",
  "reason": "role_missing:service:billing.read"
}
```

matt (eng-security): immediate hypothesis: a permission rename in the role map (`billing.read` -> `billing.view`) left legacy bindings broken. but why models also?

elena (eng-platform): digging audit logs — I see policy attach/detach events around deploy. also a KMS access error for the model key twice. looks like the service-role lost `kms:Decrypt` on the model key used for shared models. that would cause model access to fail even if API perms are present.

ops-bot: rollback initiated by elena - starting rollback of rbac-refactor v2 (step 1/3) :arrows_counterclockwise:

matt (eng-security): ok rollback in progress. I added a temporary compatibility mapping to translate `billing.view` -> `billing.read` for bindings so existing orgs don't lose access while we patch assignment logic.

sophie (support): ACME CSM confirmed they can login to console again and can list models. they still couldn't view billing tab for a minute but now appears fixed — CSM will do a final verify with customer.

carla (devex): audit trail snippet: 
```
2024-04-30T09:18:45Z policy.detach role:org-123:old-billing
2024-04-30T09:18:47Z policy.attach role:org-123:new-billing
2024-04-30T09:19:10Z kms:Decrypt failed for key:projects/redwood/keys/models-shared (principal:service-role)
```

matt (eng-security): root cause summary: 1) RBAC refactor renamed a couple of canonical permissions without creating backward-compatible aliases, 2) the deployment removed one KMS grant in the service-role binding by mistake, 3) combined effect caused some orgs with pinned role mappings to be unable to decrypt model keys and access billing endpoints.

elena (eng-platform): rollback completed at 09:21 and we re-applied the missing KMS grant. full verification run on affected clusters shows no more decrypt failures. recorded rollback job id: rb-20240430-17.

sophie (support): raising support ticket INC-2024-472 and notifying ACME. saving convo for postmortem. CSM will share logs with customer for transparency.

matt (eng-security): next steps: 1) patch rbac-refactor to add compatibility aliases and a migration plan, 2) add an automated smoke test in deploy pipeline that verifies KMS grants for service-role keys, 3) add runbook entry for customer lockout (how to do emergency compatibility mapping & KMS restore). I'll own the postmortem doc.

carla (devex): also created a temporary console endpoint that shows effective permissions per-user (`/admin/effective-perms?org=ACME`) so CSMs can quickly diagnose if bindings are missing.

ops-bot: incident INC-2024-472 created by sophie (support) - severity P2. link: https://redwood/incidents/INC-2024-472

matt (eng-security): thanks team. adding this to the weekly security retro and tagging platform for follow-up. :thumbsup:

sophie (support): ACME confirmed access restored and thanked us. closing the immediate escalation; will wait for matt's postmortem for the long-term fixes.
